title.en: South Korea shortens war games with US, citing Washington request
title.zh: 韩国援引华盛顿要求缩短与美国的军演

summary.en: It comes after Trump announced plans to curtail joint military exercises with South Korea, citing a "very good" relationship with North Korea's Kim Jong Un.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
South Korea's annual joint military drills with the US will be cut short by six days at the request of Washington, its defence ministry has announced.

Seoul said that the "period and scale" of the 2026 Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise had been adjusted due to a "proposal of the US side".

It comes after Donald Trump announced plans to curtail exercises with South Korea, citing his "very good" relationship with North Korea's Kim Jong Un. He also accused Seoul of refusing to take part in action against Iran.

South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun told a parliamentary hearing that neither South Korean nor US officials had been aware in advance about Trump's plans.

The combined field training exercise component of the drills would also be "partially reduced in scale", Seoul said, noting that the "specific details" of that reduction are still under discussion.

The unprecedented curtailing shakes South Korea's confidence in America's commitment to come to its aid, under a defence pact that is the foundation of their relationship.

It also sends a similar signal to other US allies in the region like Japan and Taiwan.

Wednesday's announcement comes after US officials told the Wall Street Journal that Trump is pushing his aides for a meeting with Kim Jong Un.

Pyongyang has not officially commented but the North Korean leader's sister Kim Yo-Jong said on Wednesday, "There is nothing I know about the news from Washington that there was communication between the leaders of DPRK and the US".

She also added that the reduction of the drill was not "something that merits comment".

"Just because the scale or the length is reduced, [this] does not mean that the hostile and aggressive essence of the drill changes," she was quoted as saying in state media.

While she admitted her brother personally had "good memories and view of Trump" and the relationship between the two was "firmly sound", she stressed the US had not shifted its "hostile policy" against North Korea.

Over the weekend, Trump wrote on Truth Social: "These exercises are not only costly, with much of these costs paid for by the United States of America (as usual!), but send a signal that is totally inappropriate and hostile."

He added: "While somewhat unrelated (?), I recently asked the President of South Korea if they would like to join us in the Denuclearization of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and they said, 'No thanks!'"

Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office on Monday, the president again explicitly linked his decision to South Korea's refusal to "give us a little hand" with Iran.

"We have 39,000 soldiers over there guarding you from Kim Jong Un, your next door neighbour, and you're not going to help us on a very easy military operation in Iran," he said. "That's strange".

title.en: Israel confirms it opened fire on vehicle carrying five-year-old Hind Rajab in Gaza
title.zh: 以色列证实在加沙向载有五岁儿童 Hind Rajab 的车辆开火

summary.en: She initially survived the attack but her body was recovered days later in Gaza City in 2024.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Israeli military has confirmed for the first time that it opened fire on a vehicle carrying five-year-old Hind Rajab and six members of her family in Gaza City during the war in Gaza.

The Palestinian child initially survived the attack in January 2024 that killed several family members, but her body was recovered days later along with her relatives.

After the attack, Hind managed to answer a telephone call from the Palestinian Red Crescent Society, which lasted hours. An ambulance it sent to reach her – in a move coordinated with the Israeli army - was then shelled, killing two paramedics.

In a statement, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said that following a review it would be opening a criminal investigation.

"Due to alleged failures in the coordination of the movement of the Palestine Red Crescent ambulance, it has been decided to initiate a criminal investigation of the incident by Military Police Criminal Investigation Division", it said.

The IDF initially stated that none of its troops were in the area at the time of Hind's killing. However, that suggestion was soon questioned.

The IDF later said it had "conducted raids on terror targets" with forces operating in neighbourhoods in Gaza City, including Tel al-Hawa, where Hind was located.

Hind's killing was internationally condemned after a desperate recording of her speaking to paramedics was broadcast around the world.

She and her family were trying to flee the Israeli invasion of their neighbourhood in Gaza City, when their vehicle came under Israeli fire.

Hind's pleas for someone to rescue her ended when the phone line was cut amid the sound of more gunfire.

The UN cited her case in a commission of inquiry, accusing Israel of war crimes, which it denies.

Aside from the criminal investigation into Hind and her family, the IDF also said it would investigate the killing of 15 Palestinians, including medics and a UN worker near Rafah in southern Gaza last year.

In three other cases, involving the killing of seven World Central Kitchen employees in Deir al-Balah two years ago, and four employees of Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), who were killed in two incidents, the IDF said it had not found grounds for criminal investigations.

The IDF is under pressure to show it investigates itself to try to stave off international legal action, most notably from the International Criminal Court.

It aims to counter accusations that it has committed war crimes and that there is impunity for its forces.

Correction: The initial version of this story and breaking news notification said Hind Rajab was aged six. The copy was updated after it was later confirmed she was aged five

title.en: Why the US is going after the International Criminal Court
title.zh: 美国为何追查国际刑事法院

summary.en: Marco Rubio, Donald Trump's secretary of state, has announced sanctions against two members of the International Criminal Court, including its president. Rubio's pressure on the court has far-reaching consequences.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Marco Rubio, Donald Trump's secretary of state, has announced sanctions against two members of the International Criminal Court, including its president. Rubio's pressure on the court has far-reaching consequences.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio took aim at the International Criminal Court (ICC)  on Tuesday, calling it "corrupt and fatally politicized" and claiming it has "maliciously abused its authority and exceeded its mandate."

He announced sanctions against the ICC president, Tomoko Akane of Japan, and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye of Senegal. The sanctions include freezing of their US-held bank assets and largely cutting them off from the US financial system.

The ICC has been holding individuals accountable for war crimes, genocide and crimes against humanity since 2002. The court is based in  The Hague , just like the  International Court of Justice (ICJ) , which is part of the United Nations and settles disputes between states.

Unlike the ICJ, the ICC has 125 members, not all 193 UN member states. The US, Russia and China are among the countries that have not joined, along with several states in Asia and North Africa.

Rubio  had recently threatened to dismantle the court "brick by brick." In a statement in July, the State Department outlined a number of measures Washington is considering as part of its campaign against the court. These include visa restrictions on ICC staff and tougher sanctions targeting the court and affiliated organizations. It also suggested increased scrutiny of countries "that refuse to reject the ICC's illegitimate authority" while continuing to receive US assistance.

The US has clashed with the ICC before . But legal experts around the world say Washington's latest escalation marks a significant shift.

"What the US and Marco Rubio have now essentially done is make public something that has been going on for more than a year," Andreas Schüller, co-director of the International Crimes and Legal Accountability Program at the European Center for Constitutional and Human Rights (ECCHR) in Berlin, told DW in July.

"The US has been using various forms of diplomatic pressure against other countries in an effort to change their positions, and in some cases their voting behavior, toward the ICC," he added.

"The fact that it is now being declared a campaign shows that it is being pursued strategically, that it is broader in scope, and that other countries — including those that are not ICC members — are also being brought on board to help apply pressure."

title.en: Six tourists and pilot killed in Kenya helicopter crash
title.zh: 肯尼亚直升机失事 六名游客和飞行员丧生

summary.en: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Department tells the BBC the nationalities are yet to be confirmed.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Six tourists and a pilot have been killed after a helicopter crashed at Mount Ololokwe in central Kenya, air accident officials have told the BBC.

The Aircraft Accident Investigation Department said the nationalities of the pilot and passengers were yet to be confirmed.

The Kenya Civil Aviation Authority (KCAA) said the accident happened in Samburu county at approximately 09:13 local time (06:13 GMT).

It said the helicopter was on a scenic flight from a wildlife conservancy in Loisaba to Ewaso Nyiro, a river that flows along several national reserves.

The Kenya Red Cross has told the BBC that the area is not yet accessible, but drones are being used to assess the scene.

The KCAA said the accident involved a Eurocopter EC130 B4 and it was co-ordinating operations.

The transport ministry and Air Accident Investigations Department would lead "investigations into the circumstances surrounding the accident", it added.

Samburu county is a popular tourist destination with many private wildlife conservancies and is renowned for its stunning scenery.

In February, a helicopter crash in the Rift Valley county of Nandi killed six people, including a member of parliament.

In 2024, the military chief, Gen Francis Omondi Ogolla, died after an army helicopter that was carrying 11 people crashed in the west of the country, with only two survivors.

In June 2021 at least 10 soldiers were killed when their helicopter crashed while landing near the capital, Nairobi.

title.en: Pakistan: Could ex-PM Imran Khan make a new deal?
title.zh: 巴基斯坦：前总理伊姆兰·汗能否达成新协议？

summary.en: The imprisoned former prime minister of Pakistan was moved to a hospital for medical treatment, ushering speculation over the possibility of new political negotiations.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The imprisoned former prime minister of Pakistan was moved to a hospital for medical treatment, ushering speculation over the possibility of new political negotiations.

Pakistan's Supreme Court on Tuesday ordered jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan to be shifted to a private hospital after Khan's family and political supporters repeatedly raised concerns about the 73 year old's deteriorating health in Rawalpindi's Adiala jail. 

The founder of the opposition party Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) has been imprisoned since August 2023 and is currently serving a 14-year sentence on corruption charges he says are politically motivated.

The former prime minister was ousted in a parliamentary no-confidence vote in April 2022. Khan and his supporters say Pakistan's influential military is trying to keep him out of politics, an allegation the military denies.

Despite his remaining behind bars, Khan remains politically popular. Despite a crackdown on the PTI following Khan's arrest, the candidates backed by him performed strongly in the February 2024 elections.

"Three years in prison have not removed Khan from Pakistani politics. He remains PTI's biggest political asset, but the party's reliance on him has also exposed weaknesses in its leadership and organization," Raza Rumi, a US-based Pakistani political analyst, told DW.

The transfer of Khan to the Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad for medical assessment has added a new dimension to the debate over his future and the possibility of political negotiations.

However, Khan's adviser Sayed Zulfi Bukhari rejected speculation that court decision was the result of any political deal with the government.

"There is no deal between Imran Khan and anyone. This is the Supreme Court's decision, which is very much welcomed," Bukhari said.

Pakistan's Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said in a video statement issued on Tuesday night that the government would challenge the Supreme Court order , claiming it was unlawful.

The minister said a convicted prisoner must be treated inside the jail or at a public hospital according to law, adding that he was requesting Khan's medical tests be carried out at a government hospital instead of a private facility.

"Legally, Khan has not been granted bail nor have his convictions been suspended. He will remain a prisoner, and the hospital executive ward shall serve as a sub-jail. Unfortunately, most ordinary prisoners with far more serious ailments are never allowed such facilities by the courts," Osama Malik, a legal expert, told DW. 

Pakistan's Minister of State for Interior, Talal Chaudhry, told DW that "Khan's cases will be decided by the courts."

body.zh: 被监禁的巴基斯坦前总理被转移到医院接受治疗，引发了人们对新政治谈判可能性的猜测。 巴基斯坦最高法院周二下令将被监禁的前总理伊姆兰·汗转移到一家私立医院，此前汗的家人和政治支持者多次对这位 73 岁的前总理伊姆兰·汗在拉瓦尔品第阿迪亚拉监狱中健康状况恶化表示担忧。 反对党巴基斯坦正义运动 (PTI) 创始人自 2023 年 8 月以来一直被监禁，目前正在服刑 14 年，罪名是他所说的出于政治动机的腐败指控。 这位前总理在 2022 年 4 月的议会不信任投票中被赶下台。汗和他的支持者表示，巴基斯坦有影响力的军方正试图让他远离政治，但军方否认了这一指控。 尽管汗仍在狱中，但他在政治上仍然很受欢迎。尽管汗被捕后 PTI 遭到打压，但他支持的候选人在 2024 年 2 月的选举中表现强劲。 驻美国的巴基斯坦政治分析人士拉扎·鲁米 (Raza Rumi) 告诉德国之声：“三年监禁并没有将汗从巴基斯坦政治中剔除。他仍然是巴基斯坦正义党最大的政治资产，但该党对他的依赖也暴露了其领导和组织方面的弱点。” 汗被转移到伊斯兰堡希法国际医院接受医疗评估，这为有关他的未来和政治谈判可能性的争论增添了新的维度。 然而，汗的顾问赛义德·祖尔菲·布哈里否认了法院判决是与政府达成任何政治协议的结果的猜测。 “伊姆兰·汗和任何人之间都没有达成协议。这是最高法院的决定，非常受欢迎，”布哈里说。 巴基斯坦法律部长阿扎姆·纳齐尔·塔拉尔在周二晚发布的视频声明中表示，政府将对最高法院的命令提出质疑，声称该命令是非法的。 该部长表示，根据法律，被定罪的囚犯必须在监狱或公立医院接受治疗，并补充说，他要求汗的医学检查在政府医院而不是私人机构进行。 法律专家奥萨马·马利克（Osama Malik）告诉德国之声：“从法律上讲，汗没有获得保释，他的定罪也没有被暂停。他仍将是囚犯，医院的行政病房将作为分监狱。不幸的是，大多数患有严重疾病的普通囚犯都不会被法院允许使用此类设施。” 巴基斯坦内政部长塔拉勒·乔杜里 (Talal Chaudhry) 告诉德国之声，“汗的案件将由法院裁决。” PTI 的布哈里告诉德国之声，汗“在……期间没有得到正确的医疗护理”。

title.en: 'Power of the purse': What Trump stands to lose in US midterm test
title.zh: “钱袋子”的力量：特朗普在美国中期选举中可能失去什么

summary.en: As midterm primaries continue with elections in several states this week, analysts are predicting a shake-up in the political landscape, indicating potential shifts in influence for former President Trump.
summary.zh: 随着本周几个州中期初选的继续进行，分析人士预测政治格局将发生变化，预示着前总统特朗普的影响力可能出现转变。

body.en:
The 2026 United States midterm elections will be a crucial test of Donald Trump's political strength, with Democrats hoping to regain control of Congress and Republicans seeking to defy the historical tendency for a president's party to lose ground halfway through a term.

The November elections will determine control of the House of Representatives and could reshape the balance of power in Washington for the final two years of Trump's presidency.

The first midterm primaries were held in March and have continued in recent months, with Alaska, Florida and Wyoming holding their primaries this week.

For Democrats, the November midterms offer an opportunity to demonstrate that dissatisfaction with Trump can translate into electoral gains and to begin rebuilding the party ahead of the next general election in 2028.

For Republicans, the elections will test whether Trump's political strength remains sufficient to protect the party from the historical midterm backlash that has affected many previous administrations.

And for Trump himself, a Democratic-controlled House could mean substantially greater scrutiny, investigations and political resistance during the final years of his presidency.

Wesley Widmaier, a professor at the Australian National University Department of International Relations, told SBS News an overall loss for Trump would restrict his influence.

"The House controls the power of the purse and is where budgets originate in the American system. A Democrat win would mean a loss of a lot of control for Trump," he said.

Ultimately, the midterms could provide the clearest indication yet of whether the political momentum in the US is shifting away from Trump and the Republican Party — or whether Republicans can defy the historical pattern and maintain their grip on Congress.

Every two years, US citizens elect all 435 members of the House of Representatives, while roughly one-third of the Senate is elected.

The House of Representatives has the special power to initiate tax bills and to impeach officials, while the Senate approves presidential appointments, such as judges and cabinet members.

Unlike in Australia, voting in US elections is not compulsory, and midterm elections — those held between presidential elections — tend to have lower voter turnout and less media attention.

But Widmaier said they still have significance for US politics and decision-making.

Historically, the president's party tends to lose ground in the House during midterm elections, he explained.

title.en: Donald Trump says no Iran talks planned, shares map showing Hormuz as 'new US territory'
title.zh: 特朗普称未计划与伊朗谈判，并分享地图将霍尔木兹海峡标为“美国新领土”

summary.en: US President Donald Trump stated that no talks with Iran are planned, while also sharing a map that depicted the Strait of Hormuz as "new US territory." Iran has maintained its stance that it will not reopen the vital waterway unless the US lifts its blockade of Iranian ports.
summary.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，目前没有与伊朗进行谈判的计划，同时他还分享了一张地图，将霍尔木兹海峡标注为“美国新领土”。伊朗坚称，除非美国解除对伊朗港口的封锁，否则不会重新开放这条重要的航道。

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump has said no talks with Iran are underway and none are scheduled, as he posted a map showing the Strait of Hormuz as a new US territory.

Trump has been pressing his threat to claim sovereignty over the crucial energy waterway as the nearly six-month-old Iran war grinds on with little sign of resolution.

Trump's envoy and son-in-law Jared Kushner had said on Monday that the US and Iran were having "very positive and active conversations", but the president denied that was the case.

"There are no talks or conversations going on, or scheduled, with the Islamic Republic of Iran. The Naval Blockade remains in full force and effect," Trump wrote on his Truth Social network on Tuesday night.

"The Hormuz Strait is open and operating. All water mines have been removed or detonated."

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

US sources told the Agence-France Presse news agency there had been "positive" discussions with the Iranians, but added that Trump had decided to wait and asked his team not to engage until Iran was ready to make a deal.

In recent weeks, there has been a lull in fighting, though the United Arab Emirates has recently accused Iran of firing two ballistic missiles — which landed at sea — targeting "maritime navigation." Iran, however, denied firing a missile toward the UAE.

Soon after, the UAE announced that "in light of regional escalations" it was halting all trade, commercial exchanges and financial transactions with Iran.

The UAE bore the brunt of Iranian missile and drone attacks in the first period of the war, but had not reported any attacks since the US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding in June that was meant to halt the fighting.

Earlier on Tuesday, Trump posted a map on Truth Social showing the Strait of Hormuz as a "NEW U.S. Territory".

Iran has effectively shut down the chokepoint , through which a fifth of the world's oil would usually transit, in retaliation for the war launched by the US and Israel in late February.

Trump revisited the idea again earlier in the week in comments to reporters in the Oval Office.

This is not the first time that Trump, faced with a foreign policy obstacle, has threatened to annex foreign territory.

Since returning to power in 2025, he has threatened to make Canada the 51st US state, seize Greenland and Cuba, and has even alluded to taking control of the Gaza Strip, without following through on any of these threats.

Before the Iran war erupted on 28 February, the Strait of Hormuz was an open waterway with free passage.

title.en: Indonesia-China naval drill raises neutrality concerns
title.zh: 印尼与中国海军演习引发中立担忧

summary.en: Indonesia's participation in a limited naval exercise with China near Taiwan has raised questions about its long-standing nonaligned foreign policy.
summary.zh: 印度尼西亚与中国海军在台湾附近举行了有限的海上演习，这引发了对其长期不结盟外交政策的担忧。

body.en:
Indonesia maintains a nonaligned foreign policy, but Jakarta's limited participation in a low-level naval exercise with China's navy near Taiwan has drawn scrutiny.

On August 12, an Indonesian frigate briefly joined a naval exercise with China's People's Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) in waters off Taiwan's east coast, with Taipei asking Jakarta for a reason why it joined the drill.

Indonesian Navy frigate KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai joined the PLAN guided-missile frigate Honghe for what Jakarta described as a "passing exercise." The maneuvers took place during Taiwan's annual Han Kuang military drill. 

An Indonesian Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson said they were fully aware that the exercise's location "made it particularly sensitive," but stressed that its vessel's presence "was simply part of its transit route back to Indonesia." According to the Taipei Times , the Indonesian vessel was returning from Vladivostok, Russia after an exercise with the Russian navy.  

Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council condemned Beijing's "provocation" after China announced the drill on August 11. Taipei also requested "further details from the Indonesian government" from its Ministry of Foreign Affairs.  

Beijing considers Taiwan to be Chinese territory and has vowed to "reunite" the self-ruled island with the mainland, by using force if necessary . The People's Liberation Army has ratcheted up pressure on Taiwan with frequent military exercises around the island, especially since former US House Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei in 2022.

Amid reactions from Taipei and Washington, the Indonesian Navy stated that its activities with the Chinese Navy were "not warfighting activities in nature" and "not intended as combat training."

Ying-Yu Lin, an associate professor at Taiwan's Tamkang University Graduate Institute of International Affairs and Strategic Studies, told DW that the Chinese exercise with Indonesia had little tactical significance.

"It wasn't as practical as a joint maritime drill, but China wanted to claim its capability in the waters," he said.

However, Ratih Kabinawa, a visiting research fellow at the Japan Institute of International Affairs focusing on Taiwan-Indonesia ties, told DW that regardless of the significance of the drills, Indonesia should have expected some reaction from Taiwan .

"Like it or not, Indonesia is now dragged into this kind of geopolitical gambit," she said.

Kabinawa added that passing exercises were among the lowest-level naval activities yet used by China to justify its intimidation of Taiwan.

body.zh: 印度尼西亚维持不结盟的外交政策，但雅加达有限地参与与中国海军在台湾附近举行的低级别海军演习，引起了密切关注。 8月12日，一艘印度尼西亚护卫舰短暂参加了与中国人民解放军海军在台湾东海岸附近海域举行的海军演习，台北向雅加达询问其参加演习的原因。 印度尼西亚海军护卫舰 KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai 与中国海军导弹护卫舰红河号一起进行了雅加达所说的“穿越演习”。这次演习是在台湾一年一度的汉光军演期间进行的。 印度尼西亚外交部发言人表示，他们完全意识到演习地点“使其特别敏感”，但强调其船只的存在“只是其返回印度尼西亚的过境路线的一部分”。据《台北时报》报道，这艘印尼舰艇在与俄罗斯海军演习后正从俄罗斯符拉迪沃斯托克返回。 中国8月11日宣布演习后，台湾陆委会谴责北京的“挑衅”。台北还要求外交部“提供更多细节”。 北京认为台湾是中国领土，并誓言要让这个自治岛屿与大陆“统一”，必要时会使用武力。特别是自美国前众议院议长南希·佩洛西 2022 年访问台北以来，解放军在台湾频繁进行军事演习，加大了对台湾的压力。 在台北和华盛顿的反应中，印度尼西亚海军表示，其与中国海军的活动“本质上不是战斗活动”，并且“无意进行战斗训练”。 台湾淡江大学国际事务与战略研究所副教授林英宇告诉德国之声，中国与印尼的演习没有什么战术意义。 他说：“这不像联合海上演习那么实际，但中国希望宣示其在该海域的能力。” 不过，日本国际问题研究所研究台印尼关系的客座研究员拉蒂·卡比纳瓦(Ratih Kabinawa)告诉德国之声，无论演习的意义如何，印尼都应该预料到台湾会做出一些反应。 “无论你喜欢与否，印度尼西亚现在都被拖入了这种地缘政治游戏，”她说。 卡比纳瓦补充说，此次演习是中国迄今为止用来证明其恐吓台湾合理性的最低级别的海军活动之一。 她说：“印度尼西亚在这方面也必须保持谨慎。”她补充说，雅加达应该“不要太天真”，认为参加与中国的“定期演习”不会引起人们的担忧……

reflection.en: In a world of complex geopolitical dynamics, nations often strive to maintain peace and neutrality. Indonesia's efforts to navigate its foreign policy amidst regional tensions reflect the ongoing challenge of living at peace with all, as far as it depends on them. Yet, as the story notes, such ventures also carry significant environmental and political risks that demand careful consideration. Yahweh's wisdom encourages us to foresee danger and take precautions, rather than rushing headlong into...

body.en: Boats carrying hundreds of people are a clear and alarming trend. But where do such large vessels come from? title.en: 'Left feeling like a burden': How the government's new NDIS changes may impact you
title.zh: “感到自己是负担”：政府新的NDIS改革可能如何影响你

summary.en: The National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) in Australia is undergoing changes, prompting concerns that these reforms may lead some participants to feel like a burden.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚的国家残疾保险计划（NDIS）即将进行改革，引发了人们的担忧，认为这些变化可能让一些参与者感到自己成为负担。

body.en:
An overhaul of the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) has passed the Senate with Coalition support, sent back to the Labor-controlled lower house to be rubber-stamped.

Analysis by the Grattan Institute suggests hundreds of thousands of people will be moved off the scheme or prevented from joining under the changes.

Applicants will be assessed in stages under a new test to determine their functional capacity.

That test is still being developed and will replace the current diagnosis-based model.

Acting CEO of peak body People With Disability Australia Megan Spindler-Smith says her community is grieving.

"There will be harm, there will be injuries. What we're talking about here is that when you reduce people's access to the supports that they need to be able to get out of bed, access the community, go to work, you ostensibly isolate people."

She says many lives will be made smaller by the reforms — which will slash social and community participation supports in half.

"The support needs don't go away when the funding is cut or when the supports are removed. They just get pushed onto either systems or other people, and that means isolation."

Since it started in 2013, the cost of the scheme has ballooned, rising to $50 billion dollars this year, and projected to hit $100 billion within a decade.

The government says its overhaul will slow the scheme’s growth and save almost $38 billion over the next four years.

Greens MPs like Jordon Steele-John say the focus on financial cost has made many disabled people feel like a burden.

“Many people, during the course of this debate, while the government has been trying to push this legislation through, have shared with me that they have felt as though they are being talked about in a way that leaves them feeling like a burden, and that is just not okay.”

Health Minister Mark Butler says reining in spending growth was necessary to safeguard the scheme's financial sustainability and social license.

"This plan puts the scheme back on track, and I'm confident, secures it for decades to come," Butler said.

"It genuinely has transformed the lives of hundreds of thousands of people, and I want to continue to see that happen for decades to come. But we know also that we need to build supports for people who were never intended to be covered by the NDIS, people with more low to moderate support needs, those sorts of second-tier supports that were envisaged by the designers of this amazing reform."

body.zh: 国家残疾保险计划（NDIS）的全面改革已在联盟党的支持下在参议院获得通过，并送回工党控制的下议院进行橡皮图章。 格拉坦研究所的分析表明，根据这些变化，数十万人将退出该计划或被阻止加入。 申请人将根据新的测试分阶段进行评估，以确定他们的功能能力。 该测试仍在开发中，将取代当前基于诊断的模型。 澳大利亚残疾人高峰组织的代理首席执行官梅根·斯平德勒·史密斯表示，她的社区正在悲痛之中。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 “会有伤害，会有伤害。我们在这里讨论的是，当你减少人们获得起床、进入社区、上班所需的支持时，表面上你就孤立了人们。” 她说，改革将使许多人的生活变得更加渺小——这将使社会和社区参与支持减少一半。 “当资金被削减或支持被取消时，支持需求并不会消失。它们只是被推到系统或其他人身上，这意味着孤立。” 自2013年启动以来，该计划的成本不断膨胀，今年已升至500亿美元，预计十年内将达到1000亿美元。 政府表示，此次改革将减缓该计划的增长，并在未来四年内节省近 380 亿美元。 乔登·斯蒂尔·约翰等绿党议员表示，对财务成本的关注让许多残疾人感到自己是一种负担。 “在这场辩论过程中，虽然政府一直在努力推动这项立法获得通过，但很多人都告诉我，他们觉得自己被谈论的方式让他们感觉自己是一种负担，这是不好的。” 卫生部长马克·巴特勒表示，为了保障该计划的财务可持续性和社会许可，必须控制支出增长。 巴特勒说：“这项计划使该计划重回正轨，我有信心在未来几十年内确保其顺利实施。” “它确实改变了数十万人的生活，我希望在未来几十年继续看到这种情况发生。但我们也知道，我们需要为那些从未打算被 NDIS 覆盖的人、有较低到中等支持需求的人提供支持，这些二级支持正是这项惊人改革的设计者所设想的。” 参议院进行了一次快速调查，收到了 4,500 多份意见书，在倡导者的持续竞选下，政府与……达成了一项协议。

reflection.en: When policy changes affect vulnerable members of society, it is crucial to ensure their dignity and voice are upheld. Yahweh calls us to speak up for those who may feel marginalized or unheard, advocating for their inherent worth and rights. Our compassion should extend to ensuring no one feels like a burden, but rather a valued part of our community.
reflection.zh: 当政策变化影响到社会中的弱势群体时，至关重要的是要维护他们的尊严和发言权。雅伟呼召我们为那些可能感到被边缘化或不被倾听的人发声，倡导他们固有的价值和权利。我们的怜悯之心应确保没有人感到自己是负担，而是我们社区中受重视的一员。

title.en: Why a 52-metre SpaceX rocket ended up off the coast of Christmas Island

summary.en: The rocket's arrival at the remote island caused a stir among the locals.

body.en:
Elon Musk's aerospace company SpaceX has retrieved a rocket that splashed down in the Indian Ocean near Christmas Island.

The space debris was towed to the remote island, about 1,500 kilometres off north-west Western Australia, on Tuesday.

"After approx. 24 days at sea, the SpaceX Recovery team successfully guided Starship to a location just off the coast of Christmas Island," the US aerospace manufacturer and launch services company said in a social media post.

"A team of SpaceX engineers is on their way to conduct additional analysis on the vehicle in calmer waters before attempting to return it to Starbase."

Locals in the remote territory reportedly lined up along the rugged coastline to catch a glimpse of the 52-metre-long rocket as it was towed in.

Photographer Chris Bray, who usually focuses on wildlife, said it was not something he ever expected to see.

"This SpaceX Starship was towed into the protected waters around Christmas Island this morning after an unusually gentle landing in the Indian Ocean almost a month ago left it unexpectedly floating and potentially recoverable instead of the usual explosion!" he said on an Instagram post on Tuesday.

Bray's aerial photos show the mostly black-coloured rocket being towed by cable attached to two large ships.

The rocket, which has three large and three small rocket nozzles, appears to have lost some of its outer coating, but was otherwise intact.

The SpaceX website said the company's Starship spacecraft and super heavy rocket were a reusable transport system designed to carry crew and cargo into "orbit, the moon, Mars and beyond".

In 2023, a large gold-coloured dome-like object was found on a beach about 250km north of Perth.

The Australian Space Agency later concluded it was an expended third stage of a polar satellite launch vehicle operated by the Indian Space Research Organisation.

In 1979, parts of NASA's Skylab space station crashed to earth near the sleepy towns of Esperance and Balladonia, triggering a global media frenzy.

body.en:
The leaders of Australia and Thailand have agreed to step up joint efforts to tackle transnational crime, while also pledging to elevate defence and trade ties.

Thailand prime minister Anutin Charnvirakul, in his first visit to Australia since he became leader in late 2025, met with his counterpart Anthony Albanese in Canberra on Wednesday.

The pair agreed to bolster mutual commitments to handle transnational crime, including tasking their law-enforcement agencies to "disrupt increasingly sophisticated global criminal networks", they said in a joint statement.

The nations will also elevate their security relationship by committing to a biannual meeting of defence ministers.

In a boost for Australia's fuel security, Albanese said his counterpart had made the "generous offer" of access to jet fuel, as energy markets experience supply-chain shocks as a result of the US-led war on Iran.

"Building on the strong economic ties is a top priority for my government," he told reporters.

"Times of uncertainty call for greater global cooperation between partners who are reliable and dependable, and friends."

In 2027, Australia and Thailand will mark 75 years since diplomatic relations were established between the two countries.

Anutin said: "I'm confident that our strategic partnership will remain an enduring foundation for Thailand and Australia ... and bring our countries and peoples even closer together."

"I extend my sincere appreciation once again to my dear Prime Minister Albanese and the Australian people for their warm hospitality."

The bid to crack down on transnational crime comes after Thailand tries to alleviate its reputation for being a hotspot for grey money — illicit capital that crosses borders.

The nation is an international hub for online scam work which fleeces millions of dollars from Australians each year.

Vulnerable Thai locals are often imprisoned by criminal syndicates on the outskirts of Bangkok to run the centres.

The Australian Federal Police was involved in a 2025 investigation that led to the arrest of five Australians, as well as United Kingdom, Canadian and South African nationals, operating a scam Bangkok "boiler room".

That announcement also came hours after Thai police confirmed the cause of death of a Thai woman allegedly murdered by an Australian man in June.

The Thai teenager, Tunchanok Donhomla, was allegedly suffocated, according to a police autopsy report seen by the ABC.

Thai police told ABC News that, on the basis of evidence collected, they now believed the investigation was reaching its completion.

title.en: Labor reveals super increase position amid 'predatory' practices crackdown
title.zh: 工党透露在打击“掠夺性”行为中超级增加立场

summary.en: The government drew a line on compulsory superannuation as it unveiled tougher consumer protections.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Labor will not increase how much superannuation employers must pay workers, instead focusing on reforms to stamp out "predatory" practices used to lure people to put retirement savings into risky investments.

The superannuation guarantee rate — the minimum percentage of a worker's earnings that employers must pay into a retirement fund — is 12 per cent, and there have been calls within Labor to raise the rate to 15 per cent.

While rebuffing the need to increase the guarantee rate, the government has doubled down on its defence of the superannuation system amid calls from One Nation to allow workers to withdraw funds before retirement to help pay off mortgages.

"There's no plans to lift the super guarantee," Assistant Treasurer Daniel Mulino, who unveiled the long-awaited consumer protection reforms on Wednesday, told ABC's Radio National.

He said raising the rate to 12 per cent was something Labor had long pushed for and that was now "putting people in a very strong position" for retirement.

Mulino detailed the long-awaited crackdown on predatory practices in an address to the National Press Club on Wednesday, after the high-profile collapses of First Guardian and Shield Master Funds in 2024 and 2025 stripped an estimated 12,000 Australians of their retirement savings.

One Nation has pushed to loosen rules around early access, while the government ruled out any rise to the compulsory super guarantee on Wednesday morning.

The reforms target "lead generators" — operators who use social media, online ads and cold calls to funnel people's retirement into high-risk schemes.

Unlicensed real-time communication about superannuation will be banned, and licensees will be required to take reasonable steps to ensure lead generation activities comply with legal requirements.

The anti‑hawking regime will also be bolstered, with stronger consent requirements, a narrower exemption for financial advisers to existing clients, and harsher penalties for breaches.

Mulino said the reforms were designed to strengthen consumer protections and disrupt "predatory and inappropriate behaviour" that led to the collapse of the Shield and First Guardian funds.

"Lead generators reaching out to these people in unsolicited ways, undertaking highly manipulative interactions to convince them that their super products were not performing well or were inappropriate, and then manipulating them into inappropriate products for them," Mulino told ABC radio on Wednesday morning.

The government previously floated the measures in a consultation paper published in April.

title.en: 'We have let down our partners and families': Suspended Sydney Swans players break silence
title.zh: “我们让我们的合作伙伴和家人失望了”：停赛的悉尼天鹅队球员打破沉默

summary.en: The club said the five players — who were named earlier on Wednesday — have been suspended for a breach of standards for being out late.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The five Sydney Swans players stood down after the club found they had breached its standards on the night they were linked to a sexual assault investigation have broken their silence for the first time.

"We are deeply sorry to everyone involved," reads a statement posted to the Sydney Swans website and attributed to all five players.

"We know we have let down our partners and families, members, supporters, teammates, the AFLW team, corporate partners and everyone at the Club and in the wider community."

"We accept the Club sanction and apologise for the impact this has had on those involved."

Sydney Swans chairman Andrew Pridham earlier apologised to the club's fans and corporate partners over the conduct of the five players.

But he did not apologise to the women affected in the incident, confirming the club had made no contact with them as it was a "police matter".

Pridham and Sydney Swans CEO Matthew Pavlich fronted media on Wednesday afternoon, hours after the club confirmed Riley Bice, Nick Blakey, Isaac Heeney, James Jordon and Chad Warner would not be considered for selection for the remainder of the season, including the finals.

The sanctions follow an incident at the Pullman Hotel in East Melbourne that is being investigated by Victoria Police as an alleged sexual assault.

Five players were linked to the investigation and have not been arrested or charged.

However, they said the sanctions were in response to their own "standards breach" — including staying out late, drinking, and "bringing women back to the hotel" — and independent of the Victoria Police investigation.

Asked directly whether the club had apologised to the women involved, Pavlich said the club would not be reaching out.

"It's a police matter, so we're not going to interfere with that by reaching out to them," Pavlich said on Wednesday afternoon.

"We are deeply concerned about their welfare and the wellbeing of those women and we offer as much support as we can."

But Pridham's own apology, delivered at the top of the press conference, was directed elsewhere.

He offered a "sincere apology to the community, to our many fans, our corporate partners, who've been amazingly supportive of us and understanding that we are attempting to deal with this matter as quickly as we can, as honestly as we can".

Pavlich said the club's AFLW team — who play a double-header alongside the men's side this weekend — were "deeply disappointed" by the incident and that "their welfare is of the utmost importance to us".
